title: 12th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 with the Speaker presiding, and a committee seat change was announced. Most of the part was question time for the Minister of Economic Development and Trade, Mohamed Saeed, who answered members on international bunkering revenue, the Hajj Corporation's planned hotel business, foreign-run small businesses, the dollar rate and inherited debt; the exchanges between the minister and opposition members were often heated. After a break (10:30 to 11:00) the preliminary debate began on a resolution by Maaroof Zakir about delays in the 4,000-flat Gedhoruveriya/Binveriya housing scheme and the order of land reclamation. The debate was still running at the end of this part. This part continues the preliminary debate on a motion by the Kendhoo member about delays in handing over the 4,000 Gedhoruveriya flats and the priority given to the Raasmale reclamation. Members from Hulhudhoo, Velidhoo, Inguraidhoo and North Hulhumale' spoke on how flats and land are allocated and on past and present government records. The debate was not finished: the chair adjourned the sitting for midday prayer and set the next sitting for 29 October. The text layer is partly garbled in the last speech, so that summary is less certain.

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: 35 members present, 12 on official travel, 6 on leave

items.title: Change in committee membership: Independent Institutions committee
items.outcome: Abdul Latheef Mohamed (Dhidhdhoo) named to the committee in place of Mohamed Mamdooh (Funadhoo) for PNC

items.title: Question to the Minister of Economic Development and Trade on international bunkering revenue and the economy
items.outcome: answered; many follow-up questions from members, debated

items.title: Question to the Minister of Economic Development and Trade on Maldives Hajj Corporation entering the tourist hotel business
items.outcome: answered; follow-up questions from members, debated

items.title: Preliminary debate: resolution on delays in the Gedhoruveriya/Binveriya flats and land scheme and the order of land reclamation (proposed by Maaroof Zakir, Kendhoo)
items.outcome: debated; continues into the next part

items.title: Preliminary debate on the Kendhoo member's motion on delayed handover of the 4,000 flats and priority given to Raasmale (continued)
items.outcome: debated, not concluded; sitting adjourned for midday prayer, debate to continue 29 Oct 2025

speakers.name: Mohamed Saeed
positions: As Minister of Economic Development and Trade, said international bunkering began in Sept 2024 and has brought about MVR 192 million income and MVR 17 million tax, per State Trading Organization figures.
Said the government works with the private sector on small-business and foreign-business rules, and that the old runway is being turned into a taxiway.
Defended the government's record and criticised the previous government's debt and money printing; said ATMs now cover 180 islands.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: In question time, asked what is being done to expand local tourism, fishing and small businesses beyond bunkering.
Presented the resolution on the 4,000-flat housing scheme, saying 585 applicants' rights were removed and many remain unserved.
Urged finishing Gulheefalhu, Giraavaru, North Thilafushi and Hulhumale Phase 3 before Rasmale, and housing the registered applicants.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked how many foreign vessels bunkering has served, total revenue so far, and when the USD 400 million earlier forecast would be reached.
Asked about maritime-linked jobs and the share of Maldivians employed.
Asked whether the MVR 125.2 billion inherited debt includes any from the minister's earlier time in government.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked about long-term steps to diversify the economy and how many billions the previous government printed.
Asked what is being done on the dollar shortage facing Maldivian traders.
In the housing debate, criticised how land and flats were handled under past governments.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked how the government will bring down the dollar rate, which traders say raises prices.
Asked about policy where a third company sells fuel on an island already served by two.
Said the 4,000 flats are unfinished with no recipient list set, and linked the delay to the state lacking money.
Argued costly new reclamation should stop while reclaimed land around Greater Malé stays undeveloped, with spending going to island services.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked why the USD 400 million forecast for the budget differed from reality and whether research was done before launch.
Asked for updates on a reported Qatari USD 8.8 billion investment, the planned financial centre, and the claim of a second runway.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked whether the government tried to stop Hajj Corporation entering the tourist hotel business and what it means for private operators.
Asked about modernising the old business portal and the status of the seaplane terminal at the Sheraton resort.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked whether members sought Hajj Corporation answers in writing, and whether the previous government's economic policy helped or harmed the economy.
Said the 4,000 flats were largely unfinished and funded by borrowing when the previous MDP government left office, and recalled allocation complaints sent to the ACC.
Said 7,000 flats of 2018 with allocation letters were cancelled, and that the current government will give flats only to rightful holders.
Argued the motion is politically motivated and questioned whether it should proceed as a motion rather than an urgent matter.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Asked the minister to consider a garment factory in Addu Hulhudhoo/Meedhoo to create local work.
In the housing debate, said housing is a basic constitutional right and criticised past governments' handling of land.
Continuing from part 1: said flats and land should reach rightful applicants, and criticised allocation through party-prepared lists and allocated flats being rented out.
Said the Raasmale reclamation is meant to give a lasting fix so every citizen can get land and a flat.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: In the housing debate, said most of the 4,000 flats were allocated and that disputed ones were halted for review.
Said about 500 flats remain unallocated and that qualifying applicants will receive them.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked whether interested parties have been found to run the port and bunkering project at Fonadhoo in Laamu.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked about reported plans to print money through the monetary authority and pension office, and its likely effect on the economy.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said businesspeople find bank and state-body rules out of step with current conditions; asked whether the government will work to change them.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked what economic activity is planned around Hanimaadhoo airport opening next month, and why the USD 400 million forecast was not met.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked when Kulhudhuffushi port will become a duty-free/bonded port, and why ATM services were not extended to islands earlier.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked how successful efforts have been to stop foreigners running small businesses under Maldivians' names.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked whether the minister believes Hajj Corporation's tourism work harms local tourism, and raised tourist arrivals and the Covid period.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said housing is a right of Malé residents and that people waiting for decades have not been served fairly.
Said flats and land should go to those in need under the law, and that promises by successive presidents have gone unfulfilled.
Said the Housing Ministry does not answer applicants' calls or letters. Speech cut short by prayer time.

decisions: Abdul Latheef Mohamed (Dhidhdhoo) named to the Independent Institutions committee in place of Mohamed Mamdooh (Funadhoo) for PNC.
Question time on items 5.1 and 5.2 ended after the allotted time.
Preliminary debate on the housing and land resolution began and continues into the next part.
Sitting adjourned at midday prayer time with the preliminary debate on the motion still open.
Next sitting set for Wednesday 29 October 2025 at 9:00.
